A memory that names a specific function, file, or flag is a claim that it existed *when the memory was written*. It may have been renamed, removed, or never merged. Before recommending it:

- If the memory names a file path: check the file exists.
- If the memory names a function or flag: grep for it.
- If the user is about to act on your recommendation (not just asking about history), verify first.

Memory is one of several persistence mechanisms available to you as you assist the user in a given conversation. The distinction is often that memory can be recalled in future conversations and should not be used for persisting information that is only useful within the scope of the current conversation.

105	### 1. How a value resolves
106	
107	#### The pipeline is one-way
108	
109	```
110	theme/foundation/*.ts   ← source of truth (Tier 1)
111	        ↓
112	zimmTokens.ts           ← DERIVED. Never hand-edit.
113	        ↓
114	--zimm-* CSS custom properties
115	        ↓
116	recipes: <name>.css.ts / theme/components/*.ts
117	        ↓
118	component JSX
119	```
120	
121	`zimmTokens.ts` imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/
122	`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid` from their owning files rather than
123	retyping values. The only literals left in it are 7 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with
124	no named-scale equivalent.
125	
126	**A Tier 1 comment is wrong about those 7.** `theme/index.ts:47` says the 15 numeric aliases
127	*"are duplicates of the named scale."* `overrideStyling.md:83-85` says 7 of them are not, and
128	`overrideStyling.md` is right: `025` (1px), `700` (28px), `1100` (44px), `1200` (48px),
129	`1300` (52px), `3500` (140px), `4500` (180px) are hardcoded in `zimmTokens.ts`; the other 8
130	derive from `spacing`.
131	
132	#### The registration reality — this is the one that breaks layouts
133	
134	`theme/index.ts` registers the Zimmermann scale as **`space` only** (line 56). `sizes`,
135	`fontSizes`, `lineHeights` and `letterSpacings` are deliberately **not** registered, because
136	registering them would restyle the base retail-react-app at ~199 call sites.
137	
138	| Prop family | Reads | Bare key like `'xl'` |
139	|---|---|---|
140	| `margin` `padding` `gap` | `theme.space` ✅ registered | correct |
141	| `width` `height` `boxSize` `min/maxWidth/Height` | `theme.sizes` ❌ not registered | **falls through to Chakra's defaults** |
142	| `fontSize` `lineHeight` `letterSpacing` | ❌ not registered | wrong value, or nothing |
143	
144	Measured blow-up range: **8×–112×**. `width: 'xl'` resolves through `theme.sizes.xl` = 36rem
145	= **576px** — that shipped, blew the footer contact icons to 576px, and destroyed the layout
146	on every page. Worse: `s`, `m`, `l` are **absent** from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
147	declarations are dropped entirely and silently.
148	
149	Typography has the same twin. `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was intended;
150	`fontSize: '4xs'` emits nothing at all.
151	
152	**Live unfixed instance:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:311` has `fontSize="l"`,
153	which emits nothing. Pre-existing, out of scope for every PR that has touched that file since.
154	`recipeGuards.test.ts` cannot reach it — it walks the registered recipe map only, and this is
155	a JSX prop. Its own `SCOPE:` note says so.
156	
157	**The rule:** on a sizing or typography prop, always the CSS var —
158	`width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`, never `width: 'xl'`. Spacing props are fine with bare keys as
159	far as *correctness* goes; house style is a separate question, below.
160	
161	#### [CORRECTED] `var(--zimm-*)` in component JSX is now required, not a smell
162	
163	An earlier revision of this document said component JSX should use `textStyle` plus semantic
164	token strings (`color="text.default"`, `padding="m"`), and that seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was
165	a signal to look closer. **That is inverted from the current rule and following it now fails
166	review.**
167	
168	`overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2 and `css.md` both state it plainly:
169	
170	```tsx
171	// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string
172	<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />
173	
174	// ✅ the raw var(--zimm-*) reference
175	<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
176	```
177	
178	The stated reason is **house style, not correctness**: a bare key resolves to the identical
179	value on a registered scale, but it forces a reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s
180	registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. A `var()` reference is
181	unambiguous at every call site.
182	
183	`textStyle` is the one legitimate bare key — there is no `var()` for the composite expansion,
184	only for its individual pieces.
185	
186	**And it can never emit one.** `zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts`, so the reverse
187	would be a circular import; `textStyle` therefore always expands to resolved literals at build
188	time. **This is correct behaviour, not a defect** — and it means roughly **85% of what an
189	emitted-CSS audit flags as "raw literals" is `textStyle` working as designed.** Read any
190	`audit:tokens` output with that in mind.
191	
192	**What survives from the old advice, and is still the main point:** brand values mostly should
193	not be in JSX at all. Re-measured on `develop` @ `269d5d4` (2026-08-29) — `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **21
194	theme files** (17 co-located `<name>.css.ts` + 4 under `theme/components/`), up from 14 as the
195	PDP work landed, and in **two** production component `.tsx` files:
196	`footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62`, a conditional `paddingLeft` that no Chakra prop
197	expresses, and `pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx`. It also appears in two
198	`.stories.tsx`, `theme/index.test.tsx` and `theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx` — stories, tests and the
199	token emitter itself are not violations and should not be counted as such. So the practice is: type via `textStyle`,
200	colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine prop-system gap.
201	
202	**[CORRECTED] The two violations named in the 25 Aug pass are fixed.**
203	`zimmProductName` and `zimmProductModelInfo` now carry no style prop at all — both route
204	everything through their `.css.ts` recipe, and `zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx` says so in a
205	docblock. The only `text.default` left in `ui-kits` is `zimmLogo/index.tsx:23`, which reads it
206	through `useToken` — the token API, not a raw literal, and not a violation.
207	
208	**Live violations right now** (`npm run audit:tokens`, 2026-08-29) are all in the header
209	surface: `header/index.tsx:238` `'240px'`, `theme/components/header.ts:73` `'597px'` and `:74`
210	`'70px'`, and `theme/components/navConstants.ts:5` `'0.02em'`.
211	
212	#### Value equality is not token equality
213	
214	Before replacing a literal with a token, three checks — all three must pass:
215	
216	1. **Same unit?** `rem` and `px` are not interchangeable. Swapping `3rem` for a px-defined
217	   alias is a **WCAG 1.4.4 regression**, not a tidy-up.
218	2. **Same semantic scale?** A spacing value and a sizing value that happen to be equal are not
219	   the same token.
220	3. **Is the target permitted?** The numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases are **class-only** —
221	   never in JSX or a recipe.
222	
223	Three real false positives died on these: `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` → `--zimm-scale-1200`
224	(check 1), `SIZE_COL_NAV` (check 2), and `SIZE_MODAL_SUB` ≡ `breakpoints.sm`, which was pure
225	coincidence.
226	
227	#### The real invariant is single-sourcing, not `var()` syntax
228	
229	Ask of any value: *is this typed more than once?* Not: *is this a `var()`?* An audit built on
230	syntax generates mostly noise.
231	
232	PR #56 reduced `foundation/`'s hand-typed literals from 237 to 64 — **173 were duplicates**,
233	the same `24px` appearing in `typography.ts` and again in `zimmTokens.ts`. Two later PRs
234	recreated that duplication one layer up without noticing: PR #52 hand-rebuilt in `sx` what
235	`textStyle="heading3"` already gave, five times; PR #55 added `cssVars.ts`, 241 lines mirroring
236	`zimmTokens.ts`'s keys as `var()` strings plus a reimplementation of seven registered text
237	styles. It was removed — a 245-line deletion; at its peak it had 10 consumer files and 148 references.
238	
239	Both misreads passed CodeRabbit. It confirmed every correctness finding and raised **zero**
240	architecture findings.
241	
242	#### Units
243	
244	- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with root font-size or browser zoom (WCAG 1.4.4) —
245	  type and spacing. Sub-pixel letter-spacing values keep a trailing `// -0.12px` comment for
246	  traceability, since they don't round to clean rem.
247	- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should *not* scale — border widths, focus-ring offsets.
248	- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts`, deliberate so media queries shift with zoom)
249	  and other genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

253	### 2. Chakra behaviours that fail silently
254	
255	Seven mechanisms. None produces an error, a warning, or a failing type-check.
256	
257	**0. Always declare your own `parts` array.** A recipe with no `parts` inherits the base's
258	list, so any Zimmermann part you add is undeclared and silently unstyled.
259	
260	**1. `extendTheme` deep-merges — it does not replace.** A recipe named `Footer` merges into
261	base SFCC's `Footer` rather than replacing it, inheriting parts you never wrote. Namespace
262	everything: `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`. `recipeGuards.test.ts` enforces this with
263	`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — those three are deliberate; anything
264	else must be namespaced.
265	
266	**1b. The merge reorders keys.** A key that already exists in the base keeps the **base's**
267	position in the merged object; a key you add that the base lacks is appended **last**. That is
268	the mechanism behind a shorthand resetting a longhand you wrote first — the order in your file
269	is not the order that ships. Inspect what actually applies:
270	
271	```js
272	theme.components.Header.baseStyle   // merged — what actually applies
273	```
274	
275	**2. A recipe unit test cannot catch the merge.** `extendTheme` does **not** populate
276	`theme.__cssMap` — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`. So a direct `css()(theme)`
277	assertion in Vitest passes vacuously against an unmerged object.
278	
279	**3. Compound values never tokenise.** Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value.
280	`padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser. Use axis props
281	(`paddingInline`, `paddingBlock`).
282	
283	**4. A shorthand declared after a longhand resets it.** `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock`
284	wipes it. Order matters; prefer the axis props throughout.
285	
286	**5. `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"`** as a style prop, merged *after* `__css`, so a `p:`
287	in your recipe size is discarded. **Size it with `minW`/`minH`** — which is also how you hit the
288	24×24 target-size requirement.
289	
290	**6. Register the recipe or destructuring throws at runtime.** Chakra resolves a recipe by the
291	string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path — so co-location is free, but the
292	key must be in `theme/components/index.ts`.
293	
294	**7. Breakpoint tokens conflict with Chakra's.** `BP.desktop` is 64em; Chakra's `lg` is 62em
295	and `xl` is 80em. A responsive array silently steps at the wrong width. Write explicit media
296	queries:
297	
298	```ts
299	[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
300	```
301	
302	The array shorthand also puts a bare token key at every step, and the guard flags all four.

306	### 3. Component structure
307	
308	#### Placement — settled
309	
310	```
311	overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx
312	```
313	
314	Being under `components/` is load-bearing for the registry generator, which scans that path.
315	
316	**Three casing families, each correct in its own context. Do not generalise between them:**
317	
318	| Family | Casing | Why |
319	|---|---|---|
320	| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | must match upstream's import path |
321	| ui-kit component | `zimmButton/` camelCase | Zimmermann-authored — the default rule |
322	| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | mirrors upstream exactly |
323	
324	Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Note the theme key is
325	PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`) while its recipe file is camelCase.
326	
327	#### Tier is by composition, not visual size
328	
329	Read it off the imports, not the DOM:
330	
331	- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit. `zimmModal` is an atom despite being portal + backdrop +
332	  `role="dialog"` chrome, because it owns no content (`maxWidth`, `labelledBy`, children all
333	  come from the caller).
334	- **molecule** — composes atoms with light local logic. `zimmInputAction` = TextInput + Button
335	  + local validation state.
336	- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**. `zimmSubscribeSection`
337	  owns the subscribe state machine.
338	
339	An icon passed as a prop doesn't count (`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom). Slotted
340	children don't count.
341	
342	**Storybook `title` is a different axis from the folder.** Folder = composition depth;
343	`title` = domain. `zimmModal` (atom) → `Elements/`; `zimmSubscribeSection` (organism) →
344	`Forms/`; `Footer` → `Layout/`. Don't conflate them.
345	
346	#### Styling surface — a registered recipe, always
347	
348	Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a plain stylesheet. The recipe may live beside
349	the component as `<name>.css.ts` or centrally in `theme/components/` — Chakra resolves by
350	string key, so this is purely organisational.
351	
352	The argument against authoring in a stylesheet is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see
353	`var(--zimm-*)`, which is **derived output at the bottom of the pipeline**. Author there and
354	you lose `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, and the theme
355	drift-guard tests. Not bad CSS — the wrong end of the pipeline.
356	
357	For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is the bridge:
358	native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`.
359	
360	**Co-location changes who reviews it.** `CODEOWNERS:186`
361	(`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only) is placed **last** among the
362	`components/` rules, and CODEOWNERS is last-match-wins, not most-specific-wins. So a `.css.ts`
363	inside `footer/` drops the Tier 2 approver requirement the surrounding directory carries,
364	while `footer/index.tsx` keeps it. The stated rationale: a co-located recipe *composes
365	established tokens*; authoring a new token still means `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1).
366	
367	`overrideStyling.md` flags its own inconsistency here rather than papering over it —
368	`zimmButton.css.ts` keys the app-wide `Button` recipe and is no longer designer-gated.
369	
370	#### No data-fetching in `components/`
371	
372	Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props. Data-fetching belongs in
373	`overrides/app/pages/` or a container.
374	
375	**One documented exception:** Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`,
376	`useUiCopy`) may be called from any component including presentational leaves, because they
377	read from a Provider mounted above the route tree. Narrow by design — content identical for
378	every consumer regardless of route, not anything that varies per page.
379	
380	**Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades:
381	`useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`, one line, renders with zero setup. **`useIntl`
382	throws** (`invariantIntlContext`), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the base SFCC `_app`,
383	not `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. Any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer
384	must wrap it.
385	
386	#### Two API patterns worth copying
387	
388	- **Encode the a11y contract in a discriminated union** so an inaccessible combination doesn't
389	  type-check.
390	- **Make an absent affordance opt-in**, not a silent default.
391	
392	#### Do not trust the registry's tier column
393	
394	`generateRegistry.mjs:133-215` hardcodes tier arrays (`TIER1_PATHS` at `:133`, `TIER2_PATHS`
395	at `:148`, squads at `:178`/`:192`), lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything else to
396	Tier 4. The registry is auto-generated and its *paths* are reliable; its
397	*tier* column is not.

421	### 4. What an override actually intercepts
422	
423	Three silent failure modes. In each, the override compiles, resolves, and never runs.
424	
425	**1. The resolver is webpack-only.** `ccExtensibility` in `package.json` redirects
426	`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` in the **real app build only**.
427	`.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to `node_modules`, and `vitest.config.ts`
428	doesn't touch it. So a base-path import of an already-overridden component builds correctly in
429	the shipped app and silently renders the **unstyled base version** in Storybook and Vitest —
430	the story looks like it's exercising your override and isn't.
431	
432	When importing a component that already has an override, use a **relative path**
433	(`'../swatch-group'`), not the base path.
434	
435	**2. A relative barrel re-export is not rewritten.** The attractive play — override
436	`shared/ui/<Name>` so branded styling propagates into base cart, checkout and account for free
437	— **does not work.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` does `export {Button} from './Button'`, a
438	relative export the resolver does not rewrite. And the consumption pattern is the wrong way
439	round: **212 base files import the barrel (195 excluding tests); 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.** The override
440	intercepts nothing.
441	
442	**3. A conditional render of an alternate module.** Overriding a component doesn't help if the
443	parent renders something else on that route. `footer` never reaches `/checkout`.
444	
445	**The generalised check**, before scoping any story around "override X and it propagates":
446	
447	```bash
448	grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
449	  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
450	```
451	
452	#### The SFCC bridge pattern
453	
454	If a component is used internally by SFCC's own base components, its **default export must
455	stay a faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour.
456	Put Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps it.
457	
458	⚠️ **No worked precedent exists in this repo.** `product-tile` is still base, `CardBaseline`
459	returns zero hits across `overrides/`, and `grep -rn forwardRef overrides/` returns one file.
460	Whoever needs this pattern first will be establishing it, not copying it.
461	
462	Where token-driven theming suffices, a theme recipe is preferable to a second export — the
463	prop-narrowing that motivated `CardBaseline` isn't needed for styling alone.

467	### 5. Figma to code
468	
469	#### The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor
470	
471	- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,
472	  `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts:
473	  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
474	- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — a delta here is a
475	  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against 45/68 was a real gap, and a naive
476	  "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.
477	
478	**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one
479	is a defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the
480	heading's cap box.
481	
482	**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.css.ts`, deriving from
483	`lineHeight` + 4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.
484	
485	#### There are two Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like
486	
487	`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).
488	Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page
489	file produced two wrong conclusions in a row — first "the slot is 59px in both states"
490	(actually `Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap
491	change 40→24: the design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix
492	that suppressed intended growth when the 68px padded box was already correct.
493	
494	#### Frames are not breakpoints
495	
496	Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024. The unframed **768–1022
497	band was genuinely broken** — 18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels — and covers three iPad
498	models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking*: the row refused to
499	break, so the words broke instead.
500	
501	#### Type metrics
502	
503	The fallback stack renders roughly **13% wider** than Futura Round, which is why serving the
504	real faces matters for parity review. `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable
505	families and is useless — compare widths instead.
506	
507	#### Measurement method
508	
509	**Subtract non-component bands before comparing totals** — the footer compares against 476,
510	not 606, once the `Disclaimer` band is excluded. **Isolate causes by cumulative in-DOM
511	mutation, one candidate at a time.** Measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports
512	frame-relative coordinates). Use
513	`domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server. Dismiss the consent banner first.
514	`Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point. **Mutation-test layout
515	fixes at mobile** — two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only because a taller sibling column masked
516	them.
517	
518	**A design nudge is still spec.** Ship it and raise the question — don't silently "correct"
519	it, and don't silently ignore it. Document the deviation at the point of use.
520	
521	#### No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect
522	
523	`width: 'xl'` resolving to 576px destroyed the footer on every page while passing `tsc`,
524	`eslint`, `vitest`, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and the Storybook a11y run. Only rendering
525	beside Figma found it.

529	### 6. Layout mechanics
530	
531	Six mechanisms, each with the fix that actually worked.
532	
533	1. **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line.** `width: min-content`
534	   resolves to the widest unbreakable run — usually what you want when a column should hug its
535	   longest word rather than its container.
536	
537	2. **`minHeight` plus `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps.** The centring
538	   discards the extra line's leading rather than growing the box. Derive height from
539	   `lineHeight` plus padding instead of reserving a `minHeight`.
540	
541	3. **An inline child inside a block parent leaks descender space.** A block-level `<li>`
542	   wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` gets a line box whose strut sits below the baseline —
543	   measured **25.5px against the anchor's own 24px**, leaking 1.5px per row (3px on a wrapped
544	   label) and making the footer's links column 9px taller than Figma's 158px.
545	   **Fix: `display: flex` on the `<li>`**, which removes the line box entirely.
546	   `footerNavColumn.css.ts:69` is the shipped instance.
547	   ⚠️ `display: block` is the **bug**, not the fix.
548	
549	4. **Give the gap to the heading, not the column.** If the design nests a group inside a stack
550	   with no gap, don't reproduce it as a sibling in a gapped flex container — the container's
551	   gap then applies where the design has none. Put the spacing on the heading's `marginBottom`.
552	
553	5. **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking.** The row refuses to break, so the
554	   words break instead. This is what broke the unframed 768–1022 band.
555	
556	6. **A non-breaking space must be the `\u00A0` escape**, not a literal character in source —
557	   invisible to review and unpredictable under reformatting. Note the dependency it creates:
558	   production copy has to carry the same character.
559	
560	**A solution window measured in single pixels is a coincidence, not a tolerance.** The footer's
561	viable column cap was **[131, 132.9) — 1.9px wide**. Treat that as a signal the constraint set
562	is over-determined, not as a fix that happens to work.
563	
564	### 7. Building against absent data
565	
566	#### Three patterns, only the first correct
567	
568	**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
569	promised; never render a control that can't act.
570	
571	- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that
572	  **keeps its margins**, measured as a roughly 64px void. It doesn't collapse; it reserves
573	  space for nothing.
574	- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
575	- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.
576	
577	#### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build
578	
579	Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:
580	
581	| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
582	|---|---|---|
583	| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
584	| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
585	| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |
586	
587	The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
588	action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
589	a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
590	information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).
591	
592	The same treatment is reused three times for "control with no action": the contact fallback,
593	`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
594	locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).
595	
596	#### Never branch on localised CMS text
597	
598	`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
599	`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
600	an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.
601	
602	#### Guarding hrefs
603	
604	Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
605	parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
606	`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**

610	### 8. CMS data and the tier reality
611	
612	New section. The footer rendered correctly in dev and was blank on the test tier, and nothing
613	in the component was wrong.
614	
615	#### Content types and entries promote by different mechanisms
616	
617	| | Content **types** (schema) | Content (**entries**) |
618	|---|---|---|
619	| Mechanism | org-scoped Environment Template | *nothing automated* |
620	| Build | `npm run sync:contentful` | — |
621	| Deploy | `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` | — |
622	
623	**A template cannot carry entries — this is structural.** The SDK type has exactly two slots:
624	
625	```ts
626	// contentful-management/dist/types/entities/environment-template.d.ts:31-34
627	entities: {
628	    contentTypeTemplates: Array<ContentTypeTemplateProps>;
629	    editorInterfaceTemplates: Array<EditorInterfaceTemplateProps>;
630	};
631	```
632	
633	No `entries`, no `assets`. The only entry-writing code in the repo is `seedRegions.mjs:71-72`,
634	which handles the 11 `region` entries and nothing else.
635	
636	#### Verified tier state, 2026-08-25
637	
638	| tier | content types | published entries |
639	|---|---|---|
640	| **dev** | **14** | **42** (+3 assets) |
641	| test / sit / uat / staging | **0** | **0** |
642	| prod | no environment id configured | — |
643	
644	The environments exist — the CDA returned `total: 0`, not `NotFound`. Nothing has ever been
645	promoted out of dev.
646	
647	**The template covers 5 of dev's 14 types** — `footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`,
648	`region`, `uiCopy`. The other 9 exist only inside the dev environment, UI-authored, with no
649	code representation, and `install:contentful` cannot move them.
650	
651	**There is no forward content promotion in this repo at all.** The actual release model is the
652	alias flip in `promoteAlias.mjs`: clone master → install template → author and verify →
653	repoint `production`/`master`. Content moves *backwards* (master → clone), never forwards.
654	
655	#### Fetch-depth is load-bearing
656	
657	`include: 3` is not arbitrary. At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved stubs,
658	`region.fields.siteId` throws, the `.catch` swallows it, and the **entire footer renders
659	nothing**. A resolution-depth mistake looks identical to a network failure from the page.
660	
661	#### Locale is not passed on any Contentful fetch
662	
663	`useContentful.ts:110` builds a URL with `content_type`, `access_token` and `include` only, so
664	the footer and `uiCopy` get the space default on all eight storefronts. Three invocation sites
665	across two production files. (`pages/experience/` and `pages/contentfulPreview/` *do* pass
666	`localeCode` — the gap is the shared hook, not every caller.) Blocked on a shared-
667	hook signature change, which is a team RFC.
668	
669	#### The check to run before promising a component works on a tier
670	
671	```bash
672	curl -s "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/<space>/environments/<env>/entries?content_type=<type>&limit=1" \
673	  -H "Authorization: Bearer <that tier's delivery token>"
674	```
675	
676	`total: 1` means it will render. `unknownContentType` means the model was never installed.
677	Note the CDA returns an unreliable `total` at `limit=0` — use `limit=1`.

681	### 9. Accessibility patterns
682	
683	Six recurring success criteria and what each actually demanded.
684	
685	- **1.1.1** — a degraded control must stay *labelled*, not `aria-hidden`. Silence is
686	  information loss.
687	- **1.4.4 / 1.4.10** — `rem` for anything that must survive zoom; a modal panel needs
688	  `maxHeight` + `overflowY` or tall content centres half-off-screen and is unreachable.
689	- **2.4.4 / 3.2.4** — no `href` and no `tabIndex` on a control that cannot act, so nothing
690	  promises an action that can't be performed.
691	- **2.5.8** — 24×24 minimum target size, which is a WCAG **2.2** addition and easy to miss if
692	  working from a 2.1 checklist.
693	- **2.5.3 Label in name** — the accessible name must *contain* the visible label.
694	- **3.2.5** — a link leaving the site gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a suffix in its
695	  accessible name. That is the project's external-link standard; it lives nowhere else.
696	- **Focus** — a programmatic `.focus()` does **not** match `:focus-visible`. A focus ring
697	  styled only on `:focus-visible` will not appear after a scripted focus move.
698	- **Portal + focus trap** — when `activeElement` is outside the trap, the trap must handle it
699	  rather than assume containment.
700	
701	Every `IconButton` needs `aria-label`; every `<img>` needs `alt` (`alt=""` for decorative).
702	Note the ast-grep rule matches `^img$` only, so Chakra's `<Image>` is invisible to it, and its
703	`aria-label` check does not match `aria-labelledby`.

707	### 10. Verification: what actually proves anything
708	
709	#### The integrity principle
710	
711	> The verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it verified, and was
712	> never made to fail on purpose.
713	
714	That is the single recurring failure mode. A green check that was never proven capable of going
715	red carries no information.
716	
717	Catalogued instances, all self-caught after reporting a false all-clear: a `safeHref` suite
718	reported "well covered, 3 layers" whose 13 cases contained **zero backslashes** — the exact
719	vector already named; a `fontFace` test iterating an empty array; a mutation test that
720	"passed" because `perl -pi` works line-at-a-time and cannot match `\n`; a recipe parity check
721	that false-alarmed three times on recipes whose `baseStyle` is a **function**; a literal-count
722	sweep that inflated 19→41 by matching `.rem` inside `removeEventListener`.
723	
724	#### Copy the non-vacuity meta-test
725	
726	`recipeGuards.test.ts` includes `test('collect() actually walks the registered recipes')`
727	precisely because every other guard asserts `toEqual([])`, which an empty input satisfies.
728	Stubbing `components` to `{}` turned the whole file green — verified.
729	
730	Same shape for layout assertions: a pure before/after equality is satisfied vacuously by a
731	collapsed container (`display:none`, `height:0`, an ancestor `display:none` — and every rect
732	is 0 in jsdom). **Anchor the measurement above zero first.**
733	
734	And resolve a function-form `baseStyle` across **all** boolean prop combinations, not the
735	default one. The original bug hid down a conditional branch a single-resolution walk never
736	entered.
737	
738	#### Green tests that encode the bug
739	
740	A suite can test *around* a defect. The region tie-break suite had a case named "order of the
741	tied candidates does not change the outcome" that used only **distinct** timestamps — the one
742	arrangement already order-independent. It passed while the bug was live.
743	
744	Mutation testing is necessary but not sufficient: it proves the check *can* fail, not that it
745	fails for the right reason.
746	
747	#### [CORRECTED] What is and is not gated
748	
749	**a11y IS gated.** An earlier belief — repeated four times in one session and again by a fresh
750	analysis this week — was that a11y is ungated because there is no `.storybook/test-runner.js`.
751	**That is Storybook 8 knowledge and is wrong for what is installed.**
752	`@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`'s `dist/setup-page-script.js:390-397` reads
753	`story.parameters?.a11y?.test` and throws when it `=== "error"`; `.storybook/preview.tsx:44`
754	sets exactly that. No `test-runner.js` is needed. **Do not delete that `preview.tsx` block.**
755	
756	Honest rider: the gate has never been made to fail on purpose, so by the standard above it is
757	**unproven, not absent**.
758	
759	**Gated nowhere at all:** `eslint`, `prettier`, `tsc --noEmit`, `audit:tokens`, any CSS bundle
760	budget, test coverage. `npm run lint` currently fails repo-wide on pre-existing prettier errors
761	and CI never notices.
762	
763	**A skipped required check counts as passing.** Live on PR #59: all four suites reported
764	`skipping` — including both *required* checks — while `mergeable: true`. `detect-changes` uses
765	`since_last_remote_commit`, and a final push touching only registry files fell outside every
766	allow-list. A 93-commit PR became merge-eligible with **zero test evidence on its head SHA**.
767	Read `gh pr checks` for `skipping`, not just for green.
768	
769	**A named gate that cannot fail:** `npm run test:contracts` is `echo 'TODO…' && exit 0`, and
770	it is a hard `needs` of `sit-gate`.
771	
772	#### Harness traps
773	
774	- **`test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.** Dev-server runs made four mutation results
775	  uninterpretable.
776	- **Vitest does not run `play`.**
777	- **jsdom always provides `window`**, so an SSR branch needs `// @vitest-environment node`.
778	- **Every jsdom rect is 0** — layout assertions there are meaningless.
779	- **`ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel, whose top-level
780	  `AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...` fails because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings here.
781	  Unfixable from a test file (`vitest.config.ts` is Tier 1). Mock at the smallest surface:
782	  ```ts
783	  vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))
784	  ```
785	  …or forward `aria-label`/`aria-hidden` when an assertion depends on the accessible name.
786	- **Portalled content is scoped to `document.body`, not `canvasElement`.** `canvasElement` is
787	  `#storybook-root`, a *sibling* of the portal target. Measured: `canvasElement.innerHTML` is
788	  41 characters, 0 dialogs inside the canvas against 1 in the document. A canvas-scoped
789	  `getByRole` fails immediately; `findByRole` fails after ~1002ms; the body-scoped form passes
790	  in 1–2ms. `testing.md:128`'s "never reach into `document`" has no portal carve-out — that is
791	  a documentation defect, not a code one.
792	- **`@storybook/test` is not installed.** `testing.md:115` prescribes it; Storybook 10 moved it
793	  to `storybook/test`. Following that line verbatim breaks.
794	
795	#### The gap no tool covers
796	
797	Duplication and reuse. No tool detects "this is a second Button." Nothing catches a bare token
798	key used as a JSX prop. Nothing catches a layout defect. Nothing catches a component whose data
799	doesn't exist on the tier it ships to.

876	from session start to merged PR.

883	
884	### 1. The Operating Principles
885	
886	#### Static-first
887	
888	Props in, markup out. A component under `overrides/app/components/` receives its data and
889	renders it. It does not fetch.
890	
891	Mock data goes in the story — never a temporary fetch you intend to remove. A component that
892	owns its own data-fetching cannot be reused where the data arrives differently: SSR-prefetched,
893	mocked in Storybook, or composed by a parent that already has it.
894	
895	**The one exception**, and it is narrow: Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks
896	(`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may be called from any component, including a presentational leaf.
897	They read from a Provider mounted above the route tree, so they don't create the
898	SSR/Storybook/composition problem the rule exists to prevent. This covers content identical for
899	every consumer regardless of route — not anything that varies per page.
900	
901	⚠️ **Their no-Provider behaviour differs and it will bite you in tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades
902	to fallback text and renders with zero setup. **`useIntl` throws**, and its `IntlProvider` is
903	mounted by the base SFCC `_app`, not `_app-config` — a narrower subtree than you'd expect. Any
904	Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer must wrap it.
905	
906	#### Leverage what already exists
907	
908	Four rungs, in order:
909	
910	1. **Use the base SFCC component as-is.**
911	2. **Override it** — mirror the path under `overrides/`, keep the kebab-case filename.
912	
913	**The default is override, not build — because an override inherits the wiring for free.**
914	Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the
915	add-to-cart modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. And because the
916	resolver rewires imports transparently, overriding a component that SFCC's own base components
917	import means **the entire base template inherits your version with zero call sites touched**.
918	
919	Worked examples: size selector → `swatch-group`; add to bag → `product-view`; max quantity →
920	`quantity-picker`; variant resolution → `use-controlled-variations` / `use-derived-product`.
921	Check what the base already does before scoping — a ticket saying "Cart API integration is in
922	scope" may be describing a call the base already makes.
923	3. **Compose existing ui-kit atoms** into something new.
924	4. **Build a new component.** Rarest. Justify it.
925	
926	Before rung 4, check the registry (`.claude/registry/`) and grep `ui-kits/`.
927	
928	**What `shared/ui` is actually for:** Contentful renderers need *primitives*, not commerce
929	components. Every Contentful component on `develop` already pulls them in — `duplexSection`
930	(`Box`, `Text`), `collectionHero` (`Box`, `Button`, `Heading`, `Text`), `hotspotPopup`,
931	`imageText`, `heroBanner`. Upstream those resolve to bare Chakra.
932	
933	⚠️ **But the barrel is not the leverage play it looks like.** Overriding
934	`shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate branded styling into base cart/checkout/account **does not
935	work** — `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` re-exports relatively, which the resolver doesn't rewrite,
936	and 212 base files import the barrel (195 excluding tests) while **0** import the individual module. See
937	Part I §4.
938	
939	#### Figma stays open the whole time
940	
941	Not at the end. **And check the Jira card's Figma link actually points at your frame** — a
942	stale link propagates: you build the wrong thing, the BA signs off against a different frame,
943	QA tests a third source. If it's wrong, ask the BA to fix the card rather than working it out
944	in a DM.
945	
946	There are **two Figma files** and cross-comparing them produces confident nonsense. See
947	Part I §5.
948	
949	#### Ask in the group chat
950	
951	Roughly 30 minutes stuck is the trigger. One question at a time.
952	
953	#### The bar you're building to
954	
955	The SOW allows **10 defects, no Sev3** — the whole project, not per sprint. (Contract figure;
956	nothing in `.docs/` records it.) Expect UI PRs
957	to be reviewed against the preview environment **and** Figma. Self-review the same way before
958	you open it (§9) — it's faster than a review round-trip.

962	### 2. Before you write any code
963	
964	#### Confirm the branch
965	
966	```bash
967	git branch --show-current
968	```
969	
970	If it's `develop` or `main`, stop. No changes.
971	
972	#### Check what already exists
973	
974	Read `.claude/registry/` for the component. The `Origin` column is what matters:
975	
976	| Origin | Means |
977	|---|---|
978	| `Custom` | Zimmermann-authored, already here |
979	| `Override` | already mirrored into `overrides/` |
980	| **`Base`** | **still upstream — you pay copy-first** |
981	
982	⚠️ **Do not trust the registry's `Tier` column.** `generateRegistry.mjs:133-215` hardcodes tier
983	arrays, lists no `ui-kits` path, and defaults everything else to Tier 4. Paths are reliable;
984	tiers are not. For what actually blocks, read `CODEOWNERS`.
985	
986	#### The three component families
987	
988	| Family | Casing | Example |
989	|---|---|---|
990	| SFCC override | kebab-case, matching upstream exactly | `product-tile/` |
991	| **ui-kit component** | **camelCase — the default for new work** | `zimmButton/` |
992	| `shared/ui` primitive | PascalCase, mirroring upstream | `Button/` |
993	
994	Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Naming a Zimmermann-
995	authored file in kebab-case falsely signals Salesforce origin — which inverts the convention's
996	whole purpose.
997	
998	#### Where a new component goes
999	
1000	```
1001	overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/
1002	  index.tsx
1003	  index.stories.tsx
1004	  <name>.css.ts          ← the recipe
1005	  index.test.tsx         ← if it has branching or event wiring
1006	```
1007	
1008	**Tier by composition, read off the imports:**
1009	
1010	- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit
1011	- **molecule** — composes atoms, light local state
1012	- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**
1013	
1014	An icon passed as a prop doesn't count. Slotted children don't count.
1015	
1016	#### What's actually overridden today
1017	
1018	Eleven directories:
1019	
1020	```
1021	_app-config  button  contentful  footer  foundation  header
1022	icons  pageContainer  product-view  ui-kits  uiCopyProvider
1023	```
1024	
1025	Still base, despite being referenced throughout `.claude/rules/`: `product-tile`,
1026	`display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu`, `seo`.
1027	**Assume most stories pay copy-first.**
1028	
1029	#### The copy-first rule
1030	
1031	For any task requiring an override that doesn't exist yet, prepare **all of them at once**
1032	before any functional change:
1033	
1034	1. Copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path.
1035	2. Convert to `.ts`/`.tsx`, update imports.
1036	3. `npx tsc --noEmit`.
1037	4. Add a temporary `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` to each.
1038	5. **Stop.** Let the user confirm the overrides are rendering.
1039	6. Remove the `console.log`s, then make functional changes.
1040	
1041	Never bundle this silently with functional work.
1042	
1043	---
1044	
1045	### 3. Design Foundations
1046	
1047	*The longest section, and the part that moves. Read it before your first component.*
1048	
1049	#### The styling hierarchy
1050	
1051	1. **`textStyle`** for anything textual — `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`. All 22
1052	   Handover text styles are registered:
1053	
1054	   `heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong`
1055	   `body2` · `mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg`
1056	   `linkSm` · `button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif`
1057	2. **`var(--zimm-*)`** for colour and spacing. The spacing scale:
1058	
1059	   | | | | | | | |
1060	   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
1061	   | `3xs` 2px | `2xs` 4px | `xs` 8px | `s` 12px | `m` 16px | `l` 20px | `xl` 24px |
1062	   | `2xl` 32px | `3xl` 40px | `4xl` 64px | `5xl` 80px | `6xl` 128px | `7xl` 160px | |
1063	
1064	   Semantic colour groups in `foundation/colour.ts`: `background` (01–07), `text`, `border`,
1065	   `status`, `link`, `icon`, `action` (`primary.*`, `secondary.*`).
1066	3. **The component's own recipe** for anything varying by variant/size/state.
1067	4. **`sx`** for a one-off prop-system gap.
1068	5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it. In practice: never. There is
1069	   no `.scss` anywhere in the footer or `ui-kits`.
1070	
1071	#### ⚠️ [CORRECTED] Rung 2 inverted — bare token strings are now wrong
1072	
1073	An earlier revision of this manual taught `color="text.default"` and `padding="m"`, and said
1074	seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was a smell. **That is backwards from the current rule.**
1075	
1076	```tsx
1077	// ❌ bare Chakra/theme token string in an override component
1078	<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />
1079	
1080	// ✅ raw var(--zimm-*) reference
1081	<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
1082	```
1083	
1084	⚠️ **Two different rules are in play and it's easy to conflate them.** A bare key on a *spacing*
1085	prop is **correct but against house style** — `theme.space` is registered, so it resolves. A bare
1086	key on a *sizing or typography* prop is **broken** — those scales aren't registered at all. The
1087	first gets a review comment; the second ships a 576px icon.
1088	
1089	The reason is **house style, not correctness** — a bare key resolves identically, but forces a
1090	reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it's correct.
1091	
1092	`textStyle` stays a bare key. It's the one exception: there's no `var()` for the composite.
1093	
1094	**In practice this rarely arises**, because brand values mostly shouldn't be in JSX at all.
1095	Measured on `develop`: `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **18 recipe files** and exactly **one**
1096	component `.tsx` — a conditional `paddingLeft` no Chakra prop expresses. Type via `textStyle`,
1097	colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine gap.
1098	
1099	#### Icon, action and motion values are constants, not theme tokens
1100	
1101	They collide with Chakra's scales the same way — `theme.sizes.lg` is 32rem and backs `boxSize`
1102	everywhere — so they are **imported directly** rather than registered:
1103	
1104	```tsx
1105	import { iconSizes, actionSizes, motion } from 'app/theme/foundation';
1106	
1107	<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />            // 20px
1108	<Button height={actionSizes.height.lg} />  // 52px
1109	```
1110	
1111	| | |
1112	|---|---|
1113	| `iconSizes` | `lg` 20px · `md` 16px · `sm` 12px |
1114	| `actionSizes` | `height.{lg: 52, md: 40}` · `paddingX.{lg: 32, md: 20}` · `gap: 16` |
1115	| `motion` | `duration.{fast: 200, default: 300, slow: 500}ms` · `easing.{standard, slides, fades}` |
1116	
1117	⚠️ **Motion values are PROVISIONAL**, pending designer sign-off — `motion.ts` says so itself.
1118	
1119	`borderWidth.default` is 1px. `focusRingOffsets.default` is 2px, `.secondary` 3px — the second
1120	exists to clear the secondary button's 1px border.
1121	
1122	#### ⚠️ The trap: a spacing key on a sizing prop
1123	
1124	**This shipped a completely broken footer, so it's worth being blunt about.**
1125	
1126	```tsx
1127	padding: 'xl',   // ✅ reads theme.space.xl
1128	width: 'xl',     // ❌ reads theme.sizes.xl = 36rem = 576px
1129	```
1130	
1131	Only `space` is registered. `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` are not.
1132	Measured blow-up range **8×–112×**. And `s`/`m`/`l` are absent from Chakra's `sizes`, so those

## Part I — UI Build: Knowledge & Context

*Why the machine behaves the way it does. Technical reference only — no roles, no process.*

*Source: `uiBuild-knowledge.md`*

Technical reference only — no roles, no process, no review workflow. Those live in
Part III (the role) and Part II (the procedure).

Every claim here was measured against the installed toolchain, not inherited from an
earlier note. Beliefs that turned out to be wrong are marked **[CORRECTED]** and the
correction is kept visible rather than silently overwritten — a claim that was confidently
wrong once is worth flagging so it isn't re-derived.

*Re-verified 2026-08-25 against `develop` @ `8362b3c` (PR #59 merged) with
`feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info` checked out.*

---

### 1. How a value resolves

#### The pipeline is one-way

```
theme/foundation/*.ts   ← source of truth (Tier 1)
        ↓
zimmTokens.ts           ← DERIVED. Never hand-edit.
        ↓
--zimm-* CSS custom properties
        ↓
recipes: <name>.css.ts / theme/components/*.ts
        ↓
component JSX
```

`zimmTokens.ts` imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/
`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid` from their owning files rather than
retyping values. The only literals left in it are 7 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with
no named-scale equivalent.

**A Tier 1 comment is wrong about those 7.** `theme/index.ts:47` says the 15 numeric aliases
*"are duplicates of the named scale."* `overrideStyling.md:83-85` says 7 of them are not, and
`overrideStyling.md` is right: `025` (1px), `700` (28px), `1100` (44px), `1200` (48px),
`1300` (52px), `3500` (140px), `4500` (180px) are hardcoded in `zimmTokens.ts`; the other 8
derive from `spacing`.

#### The registration reality — this is the one that breaks layouts

`theme/index.ts` registers the Zimmermann scale as **`space` only** (line 56). `sizes`,
`fontSizes`, `lineHeights` and `letterSpacings` are deliberately **not** registered, because
registering them would restyle the base retail-react-app at ~199 call sites.

| Prop family | Reads | Bare key like `'xl'` |
|---|---|---|
| `margin` `padding` `gap` | `theme.space` ✅ registered | correct |
| `width` `height` `boxSize` `min/maxWidth/Height` | `theme.sizes` ❌ not registered | **falls through to Chakra's defaults** |
| `fontSize` `lineHeight` `letterSpacing` | ❌ not registered | wrong value, or nothing |

Measured blow-up range: **8×–112×**. `width: 'xl'` resolves through `theme.sizes.xl` = 36rem
= **576px** — that shipped, blew the footer contact icons to 576px, and destroyed the layout
on every page. Worse: `s`, `m`, `l` are **absent** from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
declarations are dropped entirely and silently.

Typography has the same twin. `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was intended;
`fontSize: '4xs'` emits nothing at all.

**Live unfixed instance:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:311` has `fontSize="l"`,
which emits nothing. Pre-existing, out of scope for every PR that has touched that file since.
`recipeGuards.test.ts` cannot reach it — it walks the registered recipe map only, and this is
a JSX prop. Its own `SCOPE:` note says so.

**The rule:** on a sizing or typography prop, always the CSS var —
`width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`, never `width: 'xl'`. Spacing props are fine with bare keys as
far as *correctness* goes; house style is a separate question, below.

#### [CORRECTED] `var(--zimm-*)` in component JSX is now required, not a smell

An earlier revision of this document said component JSX should use `textStyle` plus semantic
token strings (`color="text.default"`, `padding="m"`), and that seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` was
a signal to look closer. **That is inverted from the current rule and following it now fails
review.**

`overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2 and `css.md` both state it plainly:

```tsx
// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ the raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

The stated reason is **house style, not correctness**: a bare key resolves to the identical
value on a registered scale, but it forces a reviewer to check `theme/index.ts`'s
registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. A `var()` reference is
unambiguous at every call site.

`textStyle` is the one legitimate bare key — there is no `var()` for the composite expansion,
only for its individual pieces.

**And it can never emit one.** `zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts`, so the reverse
would be a circular import; `textStyle` therefore always expands to resolved literals at build
time. **This is correct behaviour, not a defect** — and it means roughly **85% of what an
emitted-CSS audit flags as "raw literals" is `textStyle` working as designed.** Read any
`audit:tokens` output with that in mind.

**What survives from the old advice, and is still the main point:** brand values mostly should
not be in JSX at all. Re-measured on `develop` @ `269d5d4` (2026-08-29) — `var(--zimm-*)` appears in **21
theme files** (17 co-located `<name>.css.ts` + 4 under `theme/components/`), up from 14 as the
PDP work landed, and in **two** production component `.tsx` files:
`footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44,62`, a conditional `paddingLeft` that no Chakra prop
expresses, and `pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx`. It also appears in two
`.stories.tsx`, `theme/index.test.tsx` and `theme/zimmTokensGlobal.tsx` — stories, tests and the
token emitter itself are not violations and should not be counted as such. So the practice is: type via `textStyle`,
colour and spacing into the recipe, `var()` in JSX only for a genuine prop-system gap.

**[CORRECTED] The two violations named in the 25 Aug pass are fixed.**
`zimmProductName` and `zimmProductModelInfo` now carry no style prop at all — both route
everything through their `.css.ts` recipe, and `zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx` says so in a
docblock. The only `text.default` left in `ui-kits` is `zimmLogo/index.tsx:23`, which reads it
through `useToken` — the token API, not a raw literal, and not a violation.

**Live violations right now** (`npm run audit:tokens`, 2026-08-29) are all in the header
surface: `header/index.tsx:238` `'240px'`, `theme/components/header.ts:73` `'597px'` and `:74`
`'70px'`, and `theme/components/navConstants.ts:5` `'0.02em'`.

#### Value equality is not token equality

Before replacing a literal with a token, three checks — all three must pass:

1. **Same unit?** `rem` and `px` are not interchangeable. Swapping `3rem` for a px-defined
   alias is a **WCAG 1.4.4 regression**, not a tidy-up.
2. **Same semantic scale?** A spacing value and a sizing value that happen to be equal are not
   the same token.
3. **Is the target permitted?** The numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases are **class-only** —
   never in JSX or a recipe.

Three real false positives died on these: `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` → `--zimm-scale-1200`
(check 1), `SIZE_COL_NAV` (check 2), and `SIZE_MODAL_SUB` ≡ `breakpoints.sm`, which was pure
coincidence.

#### The real invariant is single-sourcing, not `var()` syntax

Ask of any value: *is this typed more than once?* Not: *is this a `var()`?* An audit built on
syntax generates mostly noise.

PR #56 reduced `foundation/`'s hand-typed literals from 237 to 64 — **173 were duplicates**,
the same `24px` appearing in `typography.ts` and again in `zimmTokens.ts`. Two later PRs
recreated that duplication one layer up without noticing: PR #52 hand-rebuilt in `sx` what
`textStyle="heading3"` already gave, five times; PR #55 added `cssVars.ts`, 241 lines mirroring
`zimmTokens.ts`'s keys as `var()` strings plus a reimplementation of seven registered text
styles. It was removed — a 245-line deletion; at its peak it had 10 consumer files and 148 references.

Both misreads passed CodeRabbit. It confirmed every correctness finding and raised **zero**
architecture findings.

#### Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with root font-size or browser zoom (WCAG 1.4.4) —
  type and spacing. Sub-pixel letter-spacing values keep a trailing `// -0.12px` comment for
  traceability, since they don't round to clean rem.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should *not* scale — border widths, focus-ring offsets.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts`, deliberate so media queries shift with zoom)
  and other genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

---

### 2. Chakra behaviours that fail silently

Seven mechanisms. None produces an error, a warning, or a failing type-check.

**0. Always declare your own `parts` array.** A recipe with no `parts` inherits the base's
list, so any Zimmermann part you add is undeclared and silently unstyled.

**1. `extendTheme` deep-merges — it does not replace.** A recipe named `Footer` merges into
base SFCC's `Footer` rather than replacing it, inheriting parts you never wrote. Namespace
everything: `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`. `recipeGuards.test.ts` enforces this with
`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` — those three are deliberate; anything
else must be namespaced.

**1b. The merge reorders keys.** A key that already exists in the base keeps the **base's**
position in the merged object; a key you add that the base lacks is appended **last**. That is
the mechanism behind a shorthand resetting a longhand you wrote first — the order in your file
is not the order that ships. Inspect what actually applies:

```js
theme.components.Header.baseStyle   // merged — what actually applies
```

**2. A recipe unit test cannot catch the merge.** `extendTheme` does **not** populate
`theme.__cssMap` — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`. So a direct `css()(theme)`
assertion in Vitest passes vacuously against an unmerged object.

**3. Compound values never tokenise.** Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value.
`padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser. Use axis props
(`paddingInline`, `paddingBlock`).

**4. A shorthand declared after a longhand resets it.** `padding: 0` after `paddingBlock`
wipes it. Order matters; prefer the axis props throughout.

**5. `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"`** as a style prop, merged *after* `__css`, so a `p:`
in your recipe size is discarded. **Size it with `minW`/`minH`** — which is also how you hit the
24×24 target-size requirement.

**6. Register the recipe or destructuring throws at runtime.** Chakra resolves a recipe by the
string key passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path — so co-location is free, but the
key must be in `theme/components/index.ts`.

**7. Breakpoint tokens conflict with Chakra's.** `BP.desktop` is 64em; Chakra's `lg` is 62em
and `xl` is 80em. A responsive array silently steps at the wrong width. Write explicit media
queries:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

The array shorthand also puts a bare token key at every step, and the guard flags all four.

---

### 3. Component structure

#### Placement — settled

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx
```

Being under `components/` is load-bearing for the registry generator, which scans that path.

**Three casing families, each correct in its own context. Do not generalise between them:**

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | must match upstream's import path |
| ui-kit component | `zimmButton/` camelCase | Zimmermann-authored — the default rule |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | mirrors upstream exactly |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Note the theme key is
PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`) while its recipe file is camelCase.

#### Tier is by composition, not visual size

Read it off the imports, not the DOM:

- **atom** — imports no other ui-kit. `zimmModal` is an atom despite being portal + backdrop +
  `role="dialog"` chrome, because it owns no content (`maxWidth`, `labelledBy`, children all
  come from the caller).
- **molecule** — composes atoms with light local logic. `zimmInputAction` = TextInput + Button
  + local validation state.
- **organism** — composes molecules/atoms **and owns domain state**. `zimmSubscribeSection`
  owns the subscribe state machine.

An icon passed as a prop doesn't count (`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom). Slotted
children don't count.

**Storybook `title` is a different axis from the folder.** Folder = composition depth;
`title` = domain. `zimmModal` (atom) → `Elements/`; `zimmSubscribeSection` (organism) →
`Forms/`; `Footer` → `Layout/`. Don't conflate them.

#### Styling surface — a registered recipe, always

Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a plain stylesheet. The recipe may live beside
the component as `<name>.css.ts` or centrally in `theme/components/` — Chakra resolves by
string key, so this is purely organisational.

The argument against authoring in a stylesheet is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see
`var(--zimm-*)`, which is **derived output at the bottom of the pipeline**. Author there and
you lose `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, and the theme
drift-guard tests. Not bad CSS — the wrong end of the pipeline.

For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is the bridge:
native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`.

**Co-location changes who reviews it.** `CODEOWNERS:186`
(`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only) is placed **last** among the
`components/` rules, and CODEOWNERS is last-match-wins, not most-specific-wins. So a `.css.ts`
inside `footer/` drops the Tier 2 approver requirement the surrounding directory carries,
while `footer/index.tsx` keeps it. The stated rationale: a co-located recipe *composes
established tokens*; authoring a new token still means `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1).

`overrideStyling.md` flags its own inconsistency here rather than papering over it —
`zimmButton.css.ts` keys the app-wide `Button` recipe and is no longer designer-gated.

#### No data-fetching in `components/`

Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props. Data-fetching belongs in
`overrides/app/pages/` or a container.

**One documented exception:** Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks (`useIntl`,
`useUiCopy`) may be called from any component including presentational leaves, because they
read from a Provider mounted above the route tree. Narrow by design — content identical for
every consumer regardless of route, not anything that varies per page.

**Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests.** `useUiCopy` degrades:
`useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`, one line, renders with zero setup. **`useIntl`
throws** (`invariantIntlContext`), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the base SFCC `_app`,
not `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. Any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` consumer
must wrap it.

#### Two API patterns worth copying

- **Encode the a11y contract in a discriminated union** so an inaccessible combination doesn't
  type-check.
- **Make an absent affordance opt-in**, not a silent default.

### 4. What an override actually intercepts

Three silent failure modes. In each, the override compiles, resolves, and never runs.

**1. The resolver is webpack-only.** `ccExtensibility` in `package.json` redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` in the **real app build only**.
`.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to `node_modules`, and `vitest.config.ts`
doesn't touch it. So a base-path import of an already-overridden component builds correctly in
the shipped app and silently renders the **unstyled base version** in Storybook and Vitest —
the story looks like it's exercising your override and isn't.

When importing a component that already has an override, use a **relative path**
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the base path.

**2. A relative barrel re-export is not rewritten.** The attractive play — override
`shared/ui/<Name>` so branded styling propagates into base cart, checkout and account for free
— **does not work.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` does `export {Button} from './Button'`, a
relative export the resolver does not rewrite. And the consumption pattern is the wrong way
round: **212 base files import the barrel (195 excluding tests); 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.** The override
intercepts nothing.

**3. A conditional render of an alternate module.** Overriding a component doesn't help if the
parent renders something else on that route. `footer` never reaches `/checkout`.

**The generalised check**, before scoping any story around "override X and it propagates":

```bash
grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

#### The SFCC bridge pattern

If a component is used internally by SFCC's own base components, its **default export must
stay a faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour.
Put Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps it.

⚠️ **No worked precedent exists in this repo.** `product-tile` is still base, `CardBaseline`
returns zero hits across `overrides/`, and `grep -rn forwardRef overrides/` returns one file.
Whoever needs this pattern first will be establishing it, not copying it.

Where token-driven theming suffices, a theme recipe is preferable to a second export — the
prop-narrowing that motivated `CardBaseline` isn't needed for styling alone.

### 5. Figma to code

#### The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,
  `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts:
  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — a delta here is a
  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against 45/68 was a real gap, and a naive
  "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one
is a defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the
heading's cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.css.ts`, deriving from
`lineHeight` + 4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

#### There are two Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like

`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page
file produced two wrong conclusions in a row — first "the slot is 59px in both states"
(actually `Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap
change 40→24: the design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix
that suppressed intended growth when the 68px padded box was already correct.

#### Frames are not breakpoints

Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024. The unframed **768–1022
band was genuinely broken** — 18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels — and covers three iPad
models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking*: the row refused to
break, so the words broke instead.

#### Type metrics

The fallback stack renders roughly **13% wider** than Futura Round, which is why serving the
real faces matters for parity review. `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable
families and is useless — compare widths instead.

#### Measurement method

**Subtract non-component bands before comparing totals** — the footer compares against 476,
not 606, once the `Disclaimer` band is excluded. **Isolate causes by cumulative in-DOM
mutation, one candidate at a time.** Measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports
frame-relative coordinates). Use
`domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server. Dismiss the consent banner first.
`Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point. **Mutation-test layout
fixes at mobile** — two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only because a taller sibling column masked
them.

**A design nudge is still spec.** Ship it and raise the question — don't silently "correct"
it, and don't silently ignore it. Document the deviation at the point of use.

#### No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect

`width: 'xl'` resolving to 576px destroyed the footer on every page while passing `tsc`,
`eslint`, `vitest`, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and the Storybook a11y run. Only rendering
beside Figma found it.

### 6. Layout mechanics

Six mechanisms, each with the fix that actually worked.

1. **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line.** `width: min-content`
   resolves to the widest unbreakable run — usually what you want when a column should hug its
   longest word rather than its container.

2. **`minHeight` plus `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps.** The centring
   discards the extra line's leading rather than growing the box. Derive height from
   `lineHeight` plus padding instead of reserving a `minHeight`.

3. **An inline child inside a block parent leaks descender space.** A block-level `<li>`
   wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` gets a line box whose strut sits below the baseline —
   measured **25.5px against the anchor's own 24px**, leaking 1.5px per row (3px on a wrapped
   label) and making the footer's links column 9px taller than Figma's 158px.
   **Fix: `display: flex` on the `<li>`**, which removes the line box entirely.
   `footerNavColumn.css.ts:69` is the shipped instance.
   ⚠️ `display: block` is the **bug**, not the fix.

4. **Give the gap to the heading, not the column.** If the design nests a group inside a stack
   with no gap, don't reproduce it as a sibling in a gapped flex container — the container's
   gap then applies where the design has none. Put the spacing on the heading's `marginBottom`.

5. **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking.** The row refuses to break, so the
   words break instead. This is what broke the unframed 768–1022 band.

6. **A non-breaking space must be the `\u00A0` escape**, not a literal character in source —
   invisible to review and unpredictable under reformatting. Note the dependency it creates:
   production copy has to carry the same character.

**A solution window measured in single pixels is a coincidence, not a tolerance.** The footer's
viable column cap was **[131, 132.9) — 1.9px wide**. Treat that as a signal the constraint set
is over-determined, not as a fix that happens to work.

### 7. Building against absent data

#### Three patterns, only the first correct

**Guard, then render inert but perceivable.** Never render nothing where a control was
promised; never render a control that can't act.

- **An empty-string fallback is a layout bug** — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that
  **keeps its margins**, measured as a roughly 64px void. It doesn't collapse; it reserves
  space for nothing.
- **A silent element swap actively lies** — it promises an affordance that isn't there.
- **Fix at the atom**, not at each call site.

#### The three-tier policy — the most reusable decision in the footer build

Behaviour differs by what the content *is*:

| Content class | Behaviour | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Structural** (`footerConfig`) | render **nothing** — `if (!footerData) return null` | no fallback to placeholder once wired to live data, so an outage doesn't ship stale placeholder copy to real shoppers |
| **Microcopy** (`uiCopy`) | fall back to the **English literal** | losing a button label to an outage should never blank a control |
| **Per-item destination** (a contact href) | degrade **that item only** to a labelled non-interactive `<span>` | perceivable, but no false affordance |

The per-item case is the carefully argued one: no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
action that cannot be performed (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4) — but **labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so
a screen-reader user learns the channel exists instead of getting silence (avoiding the 1.1.1
information loss an earlier `aria-hidden` caused).

The same treatment is reused three times for "control with no action": the contact fallback,
`ZimmNavItem`'s no-href branch (renders a `<button>` that doesn't navigate), and `BottomBar`'s
locale placeholder (a `<div>`, deliberately not a `<button>`).

#### Never branch on localised CMS text

`footerNavGroup` carries `showContactChannels: boolean` rather than matching
`heading === 'Contact'` — because `heading` is localised and silently stops matching the moment
an editor writes "Kontakt" or "Contacto". This footer ships to eight storefronts.

#### Guarding hrefs

Every CMS-sourced href passes `isSafeHref` before reaching an anchor. The subtlety: WHATWG URL
parsing strips C0 control characters, tab, LF and CR *before* scheme detection, so a naive
`^javascript:` regex is bypassed by `java\tscript:`. **Normalise, then test.**

### 8. CMS data and the tier reality

New section. The footer rendered correctly in dev and was blank on the test tier, and nothing
in the component was wrong.

#### Content types and entries promote by different mechanisms

| | Content **types** (schema) | Content (**entries**) |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | org-scoped Environment Template | *nothing automated* |
| Build | `npm run sync:contentful` | — |
| Deploy | `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` | — |

**A template cannot carry entries — this is structural.** The SDK type has exactly two slots:

```ts
// contentful-management/dist/types/entities/environment-template.d.ts:31-34
entities: {
    contentTypeTemplates: Array<ContentTypeTemplateProps>;
    editorInterfaceTemplates: Array<EditorInterfaceTemplateProps>;
};
```

No `entries`, no `assets`. The only entry-writing code in the repo is `seedRegions.mjs:71-72`,
which handles the 11 `region` entries and nothing else.

#### Verified tier state, 2026-08-25

| tier | content types | published entries |
|---|---|---|
| **dev** | **14** | **42** (+3 assets) |
| test / sit / uat / staging | **0** | **0** |
| prod | no environment id configured | — |

The environments exist — the CDA returned `total: 0`, not `NotFound`. Nothing has ever been
promoted out of dev.

**The template covers 5 of dev's 14 types** — `footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`,
`region`, `uiCopy`. The other 9 exist only inside the dev environment, UI-authored, with no

**There is no forward content promotion in this repo at all.** The actual release model is the
alias flip in `promoteAlias.mjs`: clone master → install template → author and verify →
repoint `production`/`master`. Content moves *backwards* (master → clone), never forwards.

#### Fetch-depth is load-bearing

`include: 3` is not arbitrary. At depth 2 the `regions` array arrives as unresolved stubs,
`region.fields.siteId` throws, the `.catch` swallows it, and the **entire footer renders
nothing**. A resolution-depth mistake looks identical to a network failure from the page.

#### Locale is not passed on any Contentful fetch

`useContentful.ts:110` builds a URL with `content_type`, `access_token` and `include` only, so
the footer and `uiCopy` get the space default on all eight storefronts. Three invocation sites
across two production files. (`pages/experience/` and `pages/contentfulPreview/` *do* pass
`localeCode` — the gap is the shared hook, not every caller.) Blocked on a shared-
hook signature change, which is a team RFC.

#### The check to run before promising a component works on a tier

```bash
curl -s "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/<space>/environments/<env>/entries?content_type=<type>&limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <that tier's delivery token>"
```

`total: 1` means it will render. `unknownContentType` means the model was never installed.
Note the CDA returns an unreliable `total` at `limit=0` — use `limit=1`.

### 9. Accessibility patterns

Six recurring success criteria and what each actually demanded.

- **1.1.1** — a degraded control must stay *labelled*, not `aria-hidden`. Silence is
  information loss.
- **1.4.4 / 1.4.10** — `rem` for anything that must survive zoom; a modal panel needs
  `maxHeight` + `overflowY` or tall content centres half-off-screen and is unreachable.
- **2.4.4 / 3.2.4** — no `href` and no `tabIndex` on a control that cannot act, so nothing
  promises an action that can't be performed.
- **2.5.8** — 24×24 minimum target size, which is a WCAG **2.2** addition and easy to miss if
  working from a 2.1 checklist.
- **2.5.3 Label in name** — the accessible name must *contain* the visible label.
- **3.2.5** — a link leaving the site gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a suffix in its
  accessible name. That is the project's external-link standard; it lives nowhere else.
- **Focus** — a programmatic `.focus()` does **not** match `:focus-visible`. A focus ring
  styled only on `:focus-visible` will not appear after a scripted focus move.
- **Portal + focus trap** — when `activeElement` is outside the trap, the trap must handle it
  rather than assume containment.

Every `IconButton` needs `aria-label`; every `<img>` needs `alt` (`alt=""` for decorative).
Note the ast-grep rule matches `^img$` only, so Chakra's `<Image>` is invisible to it, and its
`aria-label` check does not match `aria-labelledby`.
